subject: SIG: Clarifying hosting modes and evidence for Starlabs
messages:
From: Elaine Ford <elaine.ford@starlabs.com>

Subject: SIG questionnaire: hosting modes — clarifications requested

Hi Olga,

Thanks for sending the SIG spreadsheet earlier this week. Our security team reviewed the hosting section and asked for a short write-up that clearly differentiates Redwood's hosting modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC/on-prem) specifically from the SIG perspective. To be explicit, they want:

- A concise definition of each mode (2–4 bullets each).
- Where customer data can be processed & stored in each mode (network/region controls).
- Key controls that change between modes (KMS/HSM usage, tenant isolation, audit log access).
- Evidence we can attach for SOC-related items (e.g., SOC 2 report excerpts, attestation, or architecture diagrams).

I've attached the SIG worksheet with our highlights (SIG-questions-starlabs.xlsx). Can you provide the write-up and any evidence you can share? We may need to mark certain items as "customer-managed" vs "Redwood-managed" for procurement.

Also, if there's a short diagram of the network boundaries for each mode that would be ideal.

We'd like to get this to procurement by Friday Dec 11 — is that timeline realistic?

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Ford
Senior Security Analyst
Starlabs

Hi Elaine,

Thanks for the clear asks and for flagging the worksheet — appreciated. Timeline: we can get a concise write-up and a one-page diagram over to you by EOD Thursday (Dec 10) and a completed SIG workbook with supporting evidence items by Friday (Dec 11).

Quick high-level summary below; Karthik (solutions/security engineering) and Marissa (compliance lead) are looped in for the detailed evidence and attachments.

Hosted (Redwood API)
- Multi-tenant, fully-managed service hosted in our Redwood cloud regions.
- We control the serving infrastructure and manage model runtimes; customers access via API keys.
- Data processing: request data may be routed to the nearest region; customers may opt-in for region restriction for enterprise plans.
- Controls: Redwood-managed KMS, shared audit pipeline (tokenized logs), SOC 2 report covers hosted operations; limited tenant isolation compared to Dedicated.

Dedicated (Reserved capacity)
- Single-tenant GPU pools reserved for a single customer but still operated by Redwood in our infra.
- Stronger tenant isolation (dedicated queues, dedicated model instances).
- Data residency: can pin to region(s) as part of the contract.
- Controls: can integrate customer KMS for key wrapping, per-customer audit streams, SLA-backed latency/uptime.

Private / VPC / On-prem
- Customer-controlled deployment: private control plane or on-prem package; network isolated inside customer VPC or air-gapped environment.
- Customer owns infrastructure; Redwood provides a deployable package and optional remote support.
- Controls: customer-managed KMS/HSM, full access to audited logs and local storage policies; SOC 2 scope may differ and is typically covered under enterprise addendum.

I'll follow up with the one-pager and the diagram attached. Let us know if you want any items redacted for public circulation — we can provide redacted SOC excerpts or an SOC cover letter instead of full reports.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine — looping in technical details and the evidence pack. Below are explicit SIG-focused answers we typically use so you can paste them into the spreadsheet cells. Where possible I've also noted the evidence file name and the item type.

Hosted (Redwood API) — SIG annotations:
- Tenant model: multi-tenant SaaS; logical separation by account id. (evidence: SOC2-excerpt-hosted.pdf)
- Key management: Redwood-managed KMS; per-tenant key wrapping not available on standard hosted plan (evidence: KMS-ops-note.pdf)
- Audit logs: aggregated logs available via console; token-level request IDs retained per retention policy (evidence: logging-retention-policy.pdf)
- Data residency: regional routing available for enterprise; default is regional nearest routing (evidence: hosting-region-matrix.csv)

Dedicated (Reserved capacity) — SIG annotations:
- Tenant model: single-tenant compute; logical and compute isolation enforced by dedicated pools (evidence: dedicated-isolation-arch.svg)
- Key management: option to integrate customer-managed KMS for key wrapping; HSM integrations available as an add-on (evidence: kms-integration-guide.pdf)
- Audit logs: per-customer, segregated audit stream exported to customer's log collector (S3/ELK) (evidence: audit-stream-example.json)
- SLA/Operations: 99.9% uptime SLA and on-call rotation; operational runbooks are available under NDA (evidence: dedicated-sla.pdf)

Private / VPC / On-prem — SIG annotations:
- Tenant model: customer-managed environment (VPC or on-prem). Redwood control plane optional and can be deployed in customer VPC or operated offline. (evidence: private-deploy-checklist.docx)
- Key management: customer is expected to manage KMS/HSM; Redwood can provide integration guidance. (evidence: onprem-kms-checklist.pdf)
- Audit logs & eDiscovery: full access to raw audit logs and storage; retention policy controlled by customer. (evidence: onprem-logging-readme.md)
- Compliance notes: SOC 2 evidence for Redwood-hosted services covers our internal controls; for private/on-prem customers we provide mapping documents and letters of attestation where applicable.

Attachments included here: SIG-answers-v1.xlsx (completed sheet), network-diagram.svg (per-mode boundary diagram), dedicated-isolation-arch.svg (detailed), private-deploy-checklist.docx (checklist). If you need redacted SOC excerpts we can provide a short cover letter and selected pages under an NDA.

If the procurement team needs a bullet list for the contract (e.g., which responsibilities are Customer vs Redwood), here's a short table you can paste into procurement: 
- Redwood: runtime updates, model versioning, incident response (hosted/dedicated), security patching of Redwood-managed components.
- Customer: customer-managed keys (if selected), VPC/network controls, local storage retention, and access controls for private deployments.

Let me know if you want to schedule a 30-min call to walk through the architecture diagram — happy to run that with Marissa.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SIG-answers-v1.xlsx (Excel, 120 KB); network-diagram.svg (SVG, 18 KB); dedicated-isolation-arch.svg (SVG, 30 KB); private-deploy-checklist.docx (DOCX, 12 KB)
